findings.title: Benchmark workflow path filters and acceptance descriptions are incomplete
inherited_remaining: QUIC round trips are 1 to 4% slower than the default branch. No QUIC code of this project changed; the arms differ by the tokio and quinn-proto updates, and quinn-proto 0.11.19 is the security update RLS-01 requires. Which of the two costs the time has not been measured. The owner decides whether to accept that cost and re-baseline after merge.

The same candidate code measured 0.981 to 0.986 in one study and 0.959 to 0.973 in the next: the between-run spread is larger than each study's own interval, so a 5% limit will sometimes be reached by a difference this size.

The two chunk-store write metrics are disk-bound and bimodal on hosted runners (about 221 MB/s or about 1.1 GB/s in either arm, a runner disk cap); the study at 64495c4 was inconclusive on them for that reason alone. They should be measured against memory-backed storage or left out of the hosted gate.
A relative benchmark result does not establish any absolute network throughput target.

findings.title: Bounded payload buffering does not bound dense-record metadata memory
inherited_remaining: Hosted sizes stop at 1 GiB; larger logs were measured on one Windows workstation only.

The smaller buffers cost speed: about 15 to 30% on dense logs and up to a third on sparse ones (hosted runners and a 14-round workstation sweep agree on the direction; the workstation is too noisy to pick an optimum). A larger hashing batch with a small read-ahead should keep the memory limit and restore parallel hashing; that needs a quiet machine.
Returned output remains O(chunks), and the explicit offset-list APIs keep their O(records) result by design.

findings.title: A file waiting for the owner's acceptance made the sender's later files fail
inherited_remaining: What keeps this pending: inheriting an undeliverable acceptance is unit-tested but not exercised between two real daemons, and the independent read of this change was by reading, not execution.

Read from the code, not measured: once the stall deadline parks an accepted offer whose sender never returned, a different delivery of the same file is refused as resume_owned_by_another_delivery, even when the parked copy holds no bytes. The inheritance above covers only the time before that.
A waiting sender is not told when the wait ends; it finds out on its next retry.
'Accept all from this device' is remembered only until the daemon restarts; whether it should persist is an owner decision.
If an inheriting delivery is then refused for another reason (disk space, say), the acceptance is not kept and the owner is asked again. Read from the code; not exercised.
findings.current_reconciliation: Earlier Phase Zero fixed 15 consent/recovery regressions. This pass extracted the authority lifecycle without changing public API; cross-delivery parked supersession and admission-failure grant retention remain open.

findings.title: A daemon asked to stop kept running while any connection stayed open
inherited_remaining: An explicit stop now interrupts a transfer or a control command in progress instead of waiting for it, which is what it did before Python 3.12. The updater's own drain still refuses to begin while transfers are active.
The interrupt path (Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Break) is covered against real asyncio servers but not by a real-daemon test.
On Python 3.11 a closed server does not wait, so only the 3.12 lanes can fail these tests.
Not examined, by the author or the reviewer: what a stop does to a handler caught in the middle of a durable change. The stores are closed one loop turn after the connections are ended, as before.
The real-socket test of a closing connection skips on Windows, where the platform accepted all 64 MiB at once; the scripted-writer tests run everywhere.
Hosted CI on the revision with these corrections.
findings.current_reconciliation: Inherited remediation and evidence retained; no new item-specific closure claimed in this increment.

findings.title: A file sender and its receiver could each wait for the other until the send was reported as paused
inherited_remaining: Hosted CI on these revisions.

No test with real daemons fails deterministically without the first change: the stall needs a slow acknowledgement at one point in the transfer, and nothing in the product lets a test place it. The evidence with real daemons is the before-and-after count.

A sender that predates the second change still waits out its deadline when a chunk behind a held answer is refused, whatever the receiver runs. Answering what is held before every refusal would fix that for old senders and means touching about forty refusal sites; not done.
The reply wait's handling of a refusal is tested through the function it calls and a check of the source text, not by driving the daemon's send path; an independent review confirmed it by reading.

The window controller is told an acknowledgement's age when the send loop next needs room, not when the acknowledgement arrived, so chunks answered together look progressively slower and the window shrinks more often than the link warrants. Recorded, not changed: it affects speed, not completion.

The disabled QUIC chunk path derives its transfer session from the most recent inbound connection from the peer, which can be a route-verification probe. Read in the source, not tested; the path is off.
findings.current_reconciliation: Bounded ACK receipt window, correlated outstanding IDs, first local read timestamp shared by batch members, malformed/crossed-batch rejection. This eliminates stale cached ID growth and per-settlement timestamp inflation. Wire-arrival latency, disabled QUIC chunk mode and old-sender compatibility remain separately qualified.

findings.title: A daemon that had rotated its identity froze the connection of a peer that called it
inherited_remaining: Hosted CI on these revisions.

Found by reading and confirmed with the handler in isolation. It has not been exercised between two real daemons, where it needs one that has rotated and a peer that calls before the certificate is acknowledged.
It was found while looking for the cause of one hosted failure of the key-rotation live test and is not that cause: there the rotated daemon had made the call.

One more place has the same shape and was named by the reviewer without being run: a peer that becomes rejected between the accept-time check and its first frame is answered from the read task before CAPS has been received, and nothing wakes that send. It needs the owner to reject the peer in that instant, or the state store to be unavailable.
findings.current_reconciliation: Integrated newer rotation drain ordering; pre-CAPS rejection reproduced on a real socket and corrected to close without a send that waits on its own reader. Real multi-device rotation qualification remains open.
